correctness.rationale: For all real nodal data, exact step decomposition y=y0 1+sum Δy_k s^(k), constant reproduction and Jordan variation triangle inequality reduce the operator norm to max variation of the n one-step responses; each step is admissible, so this reduction is equality. For x=m+t the alternating denominator S_m=A_{m+1}(t)+A_{n−m}(1−t)>0, and alternating-tail remainder plus reflection A_inf(t)+A_inf(1−t)=π/sin πt give the C1 reciprocal approximation 1/S_m≈sinπt/π with uniform summable end-cell errors. On non-jump cells, derivative variation differs from (2/π)A_q(d) by O(d^−2+δ_m/d); harmonic double-sum bounds make total error O(1), including the one crossing cell. Summing the A_q(d) parity patterns gives a universal leading bound (2/π)H_n+O(1), while jump k=1 has main sum H_{n−1}, attaining the coefficient 2/π. Independently verified exact barycentric denominator and single-jump formulas for all tested integer n=2..15, every cell m and step k using rational t=2/5. This finite check corroborates algebra, not the uniform n→∞ remainder; the analytic tail and reciprocal estimates provide that.
residual_risks: Proposed O(1) bound relies on uniform C1 reciprocal estimates near integer poles; the proof explicitly uses removable analytic continuation on cells.
No exact finite n maximizer classification, irregular-node or high-order scheme extension.

originality.rationale: The 2010 Bos–De Marchi–Hormann paper establishes logarithmic Lebesgue (supremum-data-to-supremum-output) growth for the same rational formula, but not the discrete nodal BV-to-continuous Jordan variation norm. A separate all-fixed-positive-degree Floater–Hormann variation theorem has a related 2/π coefficient but explicitly excludes degree d=0 (Berrut) and requires different endpoint weight geometry, so it cannot by specialization supply this result. Bounded monotone overshoot in L∞ does not control accumulated oscillations; the endpoint jump's variation is a distinct derivative integral. No stronger exact Berrut BV theorem was identified in the inspected primary source material; unindexed equivalents remain possible.
residual_risks: A historical proof of BV amplification under another term (Lebesgue-type variation norms) might exist; broad older numerical-analysis literature is not exhausted.
Some other linked Berrut full manuscripts were not read end-to-end.

value.rationale: Berrut interpolation is widely used for stability; its precise discrepancy between bounded step overshoot and unbounded total oscillatory variation has clear mathematical and approximation implications. The sharp universal coefficient 2/π is not a table recomputation or an obvious consequence of the known Lebesgue coefficient: its proof exploits alternating-tail cancellation and accumulated derivative variation. Exact extremal reduction and an endpoint-adjacent asymptotic witness make this useful to BV stability analysis.
residual_risks: The result is a leading asymptotic with uniform O(1), not an exact finite-n formula.

limitations: The source CHECKER.py uses NumPy for sampled continuous variation; independent exact rational barycentric identities were checked separately, with analytic all-n proof inspected.
The true finite-n optimizing jump is not classified, and O(1) is absolute not explicit.
